sentences.text: Thalassiodracon was a small plesiosaur measuring approximately 1.5 meters in length.
This animal grew to between 1.5 and 2 meters long and possessed a skull proportionally larger than that of Plesiosaurus, accounting for one-tenth of its total body length.
It had a relatively short neck with between 27 and 31 cervical vertebrae, which is fewer than the 35 to 37 found in Plesiosaurus.
The creature possessed an unusually short skull equipped with long teeth.
The skull featured elongated teeth and very large eye orbits containing sclerotic rings.
Detailed examinations revealed a dorsal ridge on the premaxilla, a bulbous squamosal, four premaxillary teeth, and heterodont maxillary dentition.
Thalassiodracon had enlarged orbits with large, flat scleral rings, theorized to help its eyes adapt to low-light underwater environments.
Features such as elongated staples and fused exoccipital bones suggest that Thalassiodracon had adaptations for underwater hearing.
The presence of dinosaur and pterosaur bones in plesiosaur remains suggests that Thalassiodracon may have occasionally preyed on these animals.
The genus is known from complete skeletons collected by fossil hunter Thomas Hawkins in Somerset, England, in the early 1830s.
Richard Owen named the species Plesiosaurus hawkinsii in 1838, and Storrs and Taylor established the genus Thalassiodracon in 1996.
In adulthood, Thalassiodracon had forelimbs that were shorter than its hindlimbs.
Thalassiodracon had paddle-like legs for swimming and possessed a shortened tail, a trait distinguishing it from earlier ancestors.
Researchers speculate that Thalassiodracon was a pursuit predator that used speed and strength to hunt prey, based on its limb proportions.
Thalassiodracon was likely warm-blooded with a high metabolism, allowing for an active lifestyle unlike modern reptiles.
Thalassiodracon is believed to have been viviparous, giving birth to live young.
Thalassiodracon is considered one of the oldest plesiosaur representatives and may be ancestral to the superfamily Pliosauroidea.

Thalassiodracon lived in Europe from the Late Triassic to the Early Jurassic, approximately 201.6 to 196.5 million years ago.

The fossil record for Thalassiodracon spans from the Hettangian to the Pliensbachian stages, between 201.4 and 184.2 million years ago.
